properties.name: The site republishes from main after each release, dispatched by the release workflow, never from the tag
properties.rationale:
Anthony: "let's go with your recommendation (b)".

What broke (fact:root-cause-a-release-tag-cannot-publish-the-site-because-the-github-pages-environment-admits-main-alone-2026-10-14): #741 added a v* tag trigger to pages.yml, and the github-pages environment admits main alone. So v0.84.0's tag run (pages run 38555276998, attempt 1) was refused: "Tag "v0.84.0" is not allowed to deploy to github-pages due to environment protection rules." Main's run at the cut's merge counted v0.84.0 only because it started before the tag was pushed. A cut's merge always comes before its tag, so nothing guarantees that.

Why (b) and not a tag policy: main-only publishing is deliberate and stays. The release itself is the event that knows the tag exists, so it asks main to republish. A workflow_dispatch made with GITHUB_TOKEN does start a run: GitHub's "Triggering a workflow from a workflow" says events by GITHUB_TOKEN create no new run, "with the exception of workflow_dispatch and repository_dispatch". The dispatch endpoint takes Actions write, the only permission the job holds.

Where it sits: a job of its own after `publish`. By the time it runs the release is already live, so a failed dispatch turns the run red beside an untouched release. It cannot fail or undo it. A re-run of the job, or `gh workflow run pages.yml --ref main`, republishes. A dry run skips it under the same gate as every writing job.

Why corrected_cause: the class was a trigger in the repo that the environment in repository settings refuses, with nothing checking one against the other. The tests now pin pages.yml to main and to workflow_dispatch, and pin the release's dispatch to main. Both were seen failing on origin/main fb996824b (11/13) and pass with the fix (13/13).

Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: pages.yml no longer runs on a v* tag; main is the only ref that publishes reflow2's site. release.yml has a new last job, `site`, that dispatches pages.yml on main (`gh workflow run pages.yml --ref main`, with GITHUB_TOKEN) once `publish` has made the release live, so the home page's counts take in the release just cut. The job needs `publish`, carries the release's dry-run gate, holds only `actions: write`, and nothing waits on it. tools/test_release_workflow.py pins both halves; tools/site_counts.py's docstring says when the site is published.
